claim: KMS records the last successful cryptographic operation performed with each KMS key, with the CloudTrail event ID, which helps you find unused keys.
question: How can you find out whether and when a KMS key was last used?

qualifiers.condition: use of a data key outside KMS is not tracked; do not rely on last usage alone before deleting a key

evidence.quote: AWS KMS provides usage information on the last successful cryptographic operation performed with each KMS key along with the associated CloudTrail event ID. This can ease the process of identifying unused KMS keys.

claim: On 2026-04-27 KMS started to show the last cryptographic operation performed with each KMS key (timestamp, operation type and CloudTrail event ID), so you no longer need to query logs by hand, and added the kms:TrailingDaysWithoutKeyUsage condition key.
question: When did KMS start to track the last usage of every KMS key?

qualifiers.scope: all KMS keys, all Regions where KMS is available
qualifiers.condition: GA before 2026-07-15, so examinable by the book's rule

evidence.quote: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now provides visibility into the last cryptographic operation performed with your KMS keys, eliminating the need to manually query and analyze logs.
In addition, you can use the new condition key (kms:TrailingDaysWithoutKeyUsage) that enables policy-based protection against accidental deletion of recently used keys.

note: d070. The post date 'Apr 27, 2026' is on the page line 'Posted on: Apr 27, 2026'. Current truth: kms-key-last-usage-tracking.

claim: On 2024-06-13 KMS added the KEY_AGREEMENT key usage for ECC and SM2 KMS keys and the DeriveSharedSecret operation.
question: When did KMS add ECDH key agreement (DeriveSharedSecret)?

evidence.quote: | [New feature](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_DeriveSharedSecret.html) | Added new `KeyUsage` type `KEY_AGREEMENT` for NIST-recommended elliptic curve (ECC) and SM2 (China Regions only) KMS keys and added support to [derive shared secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/APIReference/API_DeriveSharedSecret.html). | June 13, 2024 |

claim: On 2025-06-13 KMS added ML-DSA post-quantum digital signatures.
question: When did KMS add ML-DSA post-quantum signing keys?

evidence.quote: | [Feature update](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/mldsa.html) | Adds support for Module-Lattice Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) post-quantum cryptographic signatures.  | June 13, 2025 |

claim: On 2025-11-07 KMS added the ECC_NIST_EDWARDS25519 key spec (EdDSA signatures).
question: When did KMS add EdDSA (Ed25519) keys?

evidence.quote: | [Feature update](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/symm-asymm-choose-key-spec.html#key-spec-ecc) | AWS KMS supports new `KeySpec` ECC\_NIST\_EDWARDS25519. | November 7, 2025 |

claim: With an external key store, you are responsible for the security, reliability, durability and performance of the keys in your external key manager, whereas for standard KMS keys AWS KMS is responsible for their security, availability, latency and durability.
question: Who is responsible for the availability and durability of keys in a KMS external key store?

values.display: the balance of responsibility shifts in your direction

qualifiers.scope: KMS keys in an external key store

evidence.quote: KMS keys in external key stores rely on key material and operations in your external key manager. As such, the balance of responsibility shifts in your direction. You are responsible for the security, reliability, durability, and performance of the cryptographic keys in your external key manager.
AWS KMS assumes responsibility for the security, availability, latency, and durability of the key material in your KMS keys.

claim: For asymmetric and HMAC keys, importing key material creates compatible keys that work both inside and outside AWS.
question: Why would you import key material into an asymmetric or HMAC KMS key?

values.display: operate within and outside of AWS

qualifiers.scope: asymmetric and HMAC KMS keys with imported key material
qualifiers.condition: you cannot import key material into keys in custom key stores

evidence.quote: For asymmetric keys and HMAC keys, importing creates compatible and interoperable keys that operate within and outside of AWS.
